title: Three in a row
prompt:
Read three integers, keep each one in its own local variable in the stack frame, and print them smallest first on one line.

The starter sets up a frame with room for three 4-byte locals at the offsets `a_s`, `b_s` and `c_s`. `scanf` needs the address of the place where it should store a number; for a frame local that address is `fp` plus the local's offset, built with `add x1, fp, a_s`. Once the three values are loaded into `a_r`, `b_r` and `c_r`, compare pairs and swap any pair that is out of order until `a_r <= b_r <= c_r`. Try your steps on an input where the smallest number comes last.

## What is checked

- the three numbers in ascending order, separated by single spaces
- the program exits cleanly
- the numbers are read into the frame (`add` present) and compared (`cmp` present)
- your program also runs on inputs you do not see: every order, negative numbers, repeated numbers, and the largest and smallest 32-bit values
starter:
// read three numbers into the frame and print them smallest first
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(a_r, w19)
define(b_r, w20)
define(c_r, w21)

a_s = 16                                    // frame offsets of the three locals
b_s = 20
c_s = 24
alloc = -(16 + 12) & -16
dealloc = -alloc

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%d"
fmt_out:    .string "%d %d %d\n"

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, alloc]!
        mov     fp, sp

        // start at 0 so the unfinished program prints 0 0 0 here and on the server
        mov     a_r, 0
        mov     b_r, 0
        mov     c_r, 0

        // TODO: read the three numbers with scanf, each into its own
        // frame local (scanf wants the local's address: fp plus its
        // offset). Load them into a_r, b_r and c_r, then compare and
        // swap until a_r <= b_r <= c_r.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     w1, a_r
        mov     w2, b_r
        mov     w3, c_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], dealloc
        ret
